paper.title_en: Revisiting the Neutrino Emission and Physical Parameter Constraints from Time-Resolved Spectra of Gamma-Ray Bursts
paper.abstract_en: The non-detection of neutrinos associated with gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) has placed significant constraints on the physical parameter space of GRB jet models. However, most of these constraints have been derived using the time-integrated spectra. In this paper, we adopt time-resolved spectra, which provide a more detailed description of the prompt emission spectral structure, to calculate the neutrino emission, and investigate how they affect the constraints on GRB physical parameters. By selecting three GRBs (i.e., GRBs 090902B, 110721A and 080916C) whose spectra are composed of different components (e.g., thermal, thermal + non-thermal, and non-thermal), we find that the expected neutrino event numbers from the summed time-resolved spectra are lower than those from the time-integrated approach in the region of relatively low dissipation radius $R$ and bulk Lorentz factor $Γ$, while the opposite trend is found at high $R$ and high $Γ$. Moreover, we also use GECAM-C data to calculate the neutrino emission of the brightest GRB 221009A, and find that the expected number of neutrino events calculated from the summed time-resolved spectra is approximately three times that from the time-integrated spectra in the high-$R$ and high-$Γ$ regime. More details of constraints on the physical parameters are also discussed. These results highlight the importance of time-resolved spectra for future GRB neutrino studies.
